title: Polynomial-time tests define languages in P
statement: Let $b$ be a Boolean-valued function on finite binary strings. If the function sending each string $z$ to the one-bit word $[b(z)]$ is polynomial-time computable, then the language of strings $z$ for which $b(z)=1$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: The Boolean-valued function $b$ on finite binary strings
replaced: Let $b : \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean test on bit strings such that the map sending $z$ to the one-bit word $b(z)$ is polynomial-time computable (computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then the language $\{z \in \{0,1\}^* : b(z) = 1\}$ belongs to $\mathsf{P}$, the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
